RagShortTexts: Palermo was a crossroads of Arab, Byzantine, and Norman art, centered in the Norman Palace.

Variants.Content: Palermo, resting in the Conca d'Oro citrus groves, forms the crowning jewel of Arab-Norman civilization. Inside the Norman Palace, the Cappella Palatina features Islamic carved muqarnas timber ceilings alongside dazzling Byzantine gold-ground mosaics. Royal edicts under Manfred are promulgated in Latin, Greek, and Arabic.
In royal tiraz textile workshops, Moorish weavers embroider gold blessings upon coronation mantles donned by Christian kings. Rational astronomy, medicine, and mathematics thrive in royal favor.
Moorish aqueducts and qanats channel cold mountain water to every lemon terrace. So long as wheat galleys sail unhindered, harbor markets overflow with dried figs, sesame cakes, and spiced sardines.
